questions.title: Gout vignette -- which pathway
questions.question: A patient develops severe pain in the right big toe, and uric acid crystals are present in his urine. This patient's pain is directly caused by the overproduction of the end product of which of the following metabolic pathways?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Pyrimidine biosynthesis produces bases used in DNA/RNA, not uric acid; its overproduction does not cause gout.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Pyrimidine degradation produces water-soluble end products (beta-alanine, beta-aminoisobutyrate), not uric acid.
explanations.C: Incorrect. De novo purine biosynthesis makes new purine nucleotides; while an overactive de novo pathway can indirectly raise uric acid downstream, the uric acid itself is the end product of the degradation (catabolism) pathway, which is what the question is asking about directly.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Purine salvage recycles existing bases back into nucleotides rather than degrading them to uric acid; a failure of salvage can indirectly raise uric acid by pushing flux toward de novo synthesis and degradation, but salvage itself is not the pathway whose end product is uric acid.
explanations.E: Correct. Uric acid is the direct end product of purine degradation (catabolism) in humans, who lack uricase. Its overproduction, or under-excretion, leads to hyperuricaemia and, when urate crystals deposit in a joint (classically the first metatarsophalangeal joint of the big toe), the acute painful arthritis of gout described in this vignette.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise acute gouty arthritis as a consequence of uric acid overproduction via purine degradation.

questions.title: Which statement best describes xanthine
questions.question: Which statement best describes xanthine?

options.B: It is oxidised to form uric acid
options.C: It is oxidised to form hypoxanthine
options.D: It is a substrate rather than a product for xanthine oxidase enzyme

explanations.A: Incorrect. Allopurinol acts as a competitive substrate/inhibitor of xanthine oxidase (it is metabolised to oxypurinol, which binds the enzyme's active site); xanthine itself does not covalently bind allopurinol.
explanations.B: Correct. Xanthine oxidase oxidises xanthine to uric acid, the terminal step of purine catabolism -- this is xanthine's defining metabolic fate. Confusing which direction the enzyme acts on xanthine is the recurring trap this question tests.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This reverses the actual direction: hypoxanthine is oxidised to xanthine (by xanthine oxidase), not the other way around; xanthine is downstream of hypoxanthine, not upstream of it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Xanthine is both a product (of hypoxanthine oxidation) and a substrate (for its own oxidation to uric acid) for xanthine oxidase -- it is not exclusively a substrate; describing it as 'a substrate rather than a product' misses that xanthine oxidase acts on it twice, at two different points in the same pathway.

questions.learning_objective: State that xanthine oxidase oxidises xanthine to uric acid, and that xanthine is both a product and a substrate of the same enzyme at different pathway steps.

questions.title: Common intermediate in purine degradation to uric acid
questions.question: A common intermediate in the degradation of all purines to uric acid is:

explanations.A: Correct. Both adenine-derived and guanine-derived purines converge on hypoxanthine before their final oxidation to uric acid: adenosine is deaminated and dephosphorylated down to hypoxanthine, while guanine is deaminated directly to xanthine (which itself derives from hypoxanthine oxidation for the adenine-derived route) -- hypoxanthine is the shared node both routes pass through en route to xanthine and then uric acid. Recognising this shared node is what lets a single enzyme, xanthine oxidase, finish off both purine bases.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Adenosine is specific to the adenine-derived route; the guanine-derived route does not pass through adenosine.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Inosine is an intermediate specific to the adenine-derived route (formed from adenosine by ADA), not a point where both purine routes converge.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ribose 1-phosphate is a byproduct released during nucleoside phosphorolysis (by PNP), not itself a purine base intermediate in the degradation sequence.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Xanthine is indeed a shared later intermediate (both hypoxanthine and guanine converge on xanthine before uric acid), but hypoxanthine is the earlier, more classically cited common intermediate on this exam's printed key.

questions.learning_objective: Name hypoxanthine as the common intermediate through which both adenine- and guanine-derived purines are degraded toward uric acid.

questions.title: Recurrent infection with low T and B cells -- enzyme's role
questions.question: A child was noted to have recurrent respiratory infection; his lab demonstrates a decrease in T and B cells. The enzyme that is defective in this patient is important in which of the following?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ribonucleotide reductase converts ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides, an unrelated enzyme not implicated in this immunodeficiency.
explanations.B: Incorrect. AMP formation is a salvage/synthesis reaction (e.g. by adenylosuccinate synthetase or adenine phosphoribosyltransferase), not the reaction whose failure causes this combined T- and B-cell picture.
explanations.C: Incorrect. UMP synthesis is a pyrimidine pathway step, unrelated to this purine-pathway immunodeficiency.
explanations.D: Correct. A decrease in both T and B lymphocytes with recurrent infection is the classic picture of adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency, one cause of severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID). ADA normally converts adenosine to inosine; without it, deoxyadenosine accumulates to toxic levels that are selectively lethal to developing lymphocytes of both lineages.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise combined T- and B-cell deficiency as pointing to ADA deficiency, and name ADA's reaction (adenosine to inosine).

questions.title: Allopurinol is an analogue of
questions.question: The drug allopurinol is an analogue of which of the following?

explanations.A: Correct. Allopurinol is structurally a hypoxanthine analogue; this structural similarity is exactly what lets it competitively engage xanthine oxidase's active site, and its own metabolite (oxypurinol) then inhibits the enzyme more durably. This structural mimicry is the pharmacological basis for allopurinol's action.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Guanine is a different purine base entirely, degraded via a separate deamination step (guanase); allopurinol's structure is not modelled on guanine.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Xanthine is xanthine oxidase's actual substrate/product, not the molecule allopurinol structurally mimics.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Uric acid is the pathway's end product, downstream of where allopurinol acts; it is not the molecule allopurinol resembles.

questions.learning_objective: Name allopurinol as a hypoxanthine analogue.

questions.title: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome -- defective pathway
questions.question: A 7-year-old boy suffers from mental retardation and self-mutilation and has increased levels of serum uric acid. These symptoms are characteristic of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, which is due to a defect in:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is a purine, not a pyrimidine, salvage disorder.
explanations.B: Incorrect. De novo pyrimidine synthesis is unrelated to this purine-salvage disease.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A xanthine oxidase defect would lower, not raise, uric acid (as seen in the rare condition xanthinuria), the opposite of this vignette's hyperuricaemia.
explanations.D: Correct. Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is caused by a near-total deficiency of HGPRT, the enzyme that salvages hypoxanthine and guanine back to their nucleotides. Loss of salvage forces purine synthesis down the wasteful de novo pathway, raising uric acid, and produces the syndrome's characteristic triad of hyperuricaemia, choreoathetosis and compulsive self-mutilation, inherited X-linked.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Purine degradation itself is intact in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome; the defect is in salvage, which secondarily increases the load going through degradation to uric acid.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the Lesch-Nyhan triad and name HGPRT deficiency as its cause.

questions.title: Allopurinol's enzyme target
questions.question: Allopurinol inhibits which of the following enzymes?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Guanase (guanine deaminase) converts guanine to xanthine; it is not allopurinol's target.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 5'-nucleotidase dephosphorylates nucleotides to nucleosides; it is not allopurinol's target.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Purine nucleoside phosphorylase cleaves nucleosides to their free bases plus ribose-1-phosphate; it is not allopurinol's target.
explanations.D: Correct. Allopurinol competitively inhibits xanthine oxidase, the terminal enzyme of purine catabolism that oxidises hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid, thereby lowering uric acid production and treating gout. This single enzyme target is why allopurinol lowers uric acid without touching the earlier salvage or de novo steps.

questions.learning_objective: Name xanthine oxidase as allopurinol's enzymatic target.

questions.title: T-cell-only immunodeficiency with normal B cells
questions.question: An immunodeficiency that affects T cells only, with normal B cells, is due to a deficiency of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency destroys both T and B lymphocytes (a combined SCID), not a T-cell-only picture.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 5'-nucleotidase deficiency is not the classic cause of a T-cell-selective immunodeficiency in this curriculum.
explanations.C: Correct. Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency lets deoxyguanosine accumulate, which is selectively toxic to T lymphocytes while relatively sparing B cells, producing a T-cell-only immunodeficiency with normal or near-normal B-cell numbers and function -- distinct from the combined T-and-B picture of ADA deficiency. Checking B-cell status alongside T-cell status is exactly how this vignette is distinguished from ADA deficiency.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Xanthine oxidase deficiency causes xanthinuria, a purine-excretion disorder, not an immunodeficiency.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish PNP deficiency (T-cell-only, normal B cells) from ADA deficiency (combined T- and B-cell SCID).

questions.title: Reaction catalysed by HGPRT
questions.question: Which reaction is catalysed by HGPRT (hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase)?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Nucleotide-to-nucleoside conversion is 5'-nucleotidase's reaction, not HGPRT's.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Guanosine-to-guanine-plus-ribose-1-phosphate is purine nucleoside phosphorylase's (PNP's) reaction, not HGPRT's.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adenosine-to-inosine is adenosine deaminase's (ADA's) reaction, not HGPRT's.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Guanine-to-xanthine is guanase's (guanine deaminase's) reaction, not HGPRT's.
explanations.E: Correct. HGPRT salvages the free base hypoxanthine directly to the nucleotide IMP, using PRPP as the phosphoribosyl donor and releasing pyrophosphate -- this single-step base-to-nucleotide salvage reaction (and the equivalent one for guanine, to GMP) is exactly what fails in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome. No other listed enzyme performs this particular one-step base-to-nucleotide conversion.

questions.learning_objective: Pair HGPRT with its specific reaction, hypoxanthine to IMP.

questions.title: Reaction catalysed by purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP)
questions.question: Which reaction is catalysed by PNP (purine nucleoside phosphorylase)?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Nucleotide-to-nucleoside is 5'-nucleotidase's reaction, a dephosphorylation, not PNP's phosphorolysis.
explanations.B: Correct. PNP cleaves a purine nucleoside into its free base plus ribose-1-phosphate using inorganic phosphate -- guanosine to guanine plus ribose-1-phosphate is the classic example, alongside inosine to hypoxanthine plus ribose-1-phosphate. This nucleoside-to-base step is exactly what fails in PNP deficiency, producing its T-cell-selective immunodeficiency.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adenosine-to-inosine is ADA's reaction, a deamination, not PNP's phosphorolysis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Guanine-to-xanthine is guanase's reaction, not PNP's.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Hypoxanthine-to-IMP is HGPRT's salvage reaction, not PNP's.

questions.learning_objective: Pair PNP with its specific reaction, a nucleoside cleaved to its base plus ribose-1-phosphate.

questions.title: Reaction catalysed by 5' nucleotidase
questions.question: Which reaction is catalysed by 5' nucleotidase?

explanations.A: Correct. 5'-nucleotidase removes the 5'-phosphate group from a nucleotide, giving the corresponding nucleoside -- the reverse direction of a kinase's phosphorylation, and the first step by which a nucleotide re-enters the nucleoside/base pool for further catabolism or salvage. This dephosphorylation step is distinct from, and runs opposite to, any kinase reaction acting on the same nucleotide.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Guanosine-to-guanine-plus-ribose-1-phosphate is PNP's reaction (acting on a nucleoside, not a nucleotide), not 5'-nucleotidase's.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adenosine-to-inosine is ADA's reaction, not 5'-nucleotidase's.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Guanine-to-xanthine is guanase's reaction, not 5'-nucleotidase's.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Hypoxanthine-to-IMP is HGPRT's reaction (the reverse direction, base to nucleotide), not 5'-nucleotidase's.

questions.learning_objective: Pair 5'-nucleotidase with its specific reaction, a nucleotide dephosphorylated to its nucleoside.

questions.title: Reaction catalysed by guanase
questions.question: Which reaction is catalysed by guanase (guanine deaminase)?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Nucleotide-to-nucleoside is 5'-nucleotidase's reaction, not guanase's.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Guanosine-to-guanine-plus-ribose-1-phosphate is PNP's reaction (acting one step earlier, on the nucleoside guanosine), not guanase's.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adenosine-to-inosine is ADA's reaction on the adenine-derived branch, not guanase's reaction on the guanine-derived branch.
explanations.D: Correct. Guanase (guanine deaminase) hydrolytically deaminates guanine to xanthine, the guanine-derived branch's route into the shared xanthine-to-uric-acid pathway. This deamination is the guanine-derived branch's mirror of ADA's action on the adenine-derived branch.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Hypoxanthine-to-IMP is HGPRT's salvage reaction, the reverse direction of catabolism, not guanase's.

questions.learning_objective: Pair guanase with its specific reaction, guanine deaminated to xanthine.

questions.title: Reaction catalysed by adenosine deaminase (ADA)
questions.question: Which reaction is catalysed by ADA (adenosine deaminase)?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Nucleotide-to-nucleoside is 5'-nucleotidase's reaction, not ADA's.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Guanosine-to-guanine-plus-ribose-1-phosphate is PNP's reaction on the guanine-derived branch, not ADA's reaction on the adenine-derived branch.
explanations.C: Correct. ADA hydrolytically deaminates adenosine to inosine, the adenine-derived branch's entry step toward hypoxanthine and, ultimately, uric acid. Loss of this reaction lets deoxyadenosine accumulate to lymphocyte-toxic levels, causing ADA-deficiency SCID.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Guanine-to-xanthine is guanase's reaction on the guanine-derived branch, not ADA's.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Hypoxanthine-to-IMP is HGPRT's salvage reaction, not ADA's catabolic deamination.

questions.learning_objective: Pair ADA with its specific reaction, adenosine deaminated to inosine.

questions.title: Reaction catalysed by xanthine oxidase
questions.question: Which reaction is catalysed by xanthine oxidase?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Nucleotide-to-nucleoside is 5'-nucleotidase's reaction, not xanthine oxidase's.
explanations.B: Correct. Xanthine oxidase catalyses the terminal oxidation of xanthine to uric acid (and, one step earlier in the same pathway, hypoxanthine to xanthine), making it the enzyme allopurinol targets to lower uric acid production in gout. This terminal step is why xanthine oxidase, not any upstream enzyme, is the pharmacological target for lowering uric acid.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adenosine-to-inosine is ADA's reaction, not xanthine oxidase's.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Guanine-to-xanthine is guanase's reaction, not xanthine oxidase's -- though its product, xanthine, is exactly xanthine oxidase's own substrate at the next step.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Hypoxanthine-to-IMP is HGPRT's salvage reaction, the opposite direction from xanthine oxidase's catabolic oxidation of hypoxanthine to xanthine.

questions.learning_objective: Pair xanthine oxidase with its terminal reaction, xanthine to uric acid.
